exercise2.hint: cut gives a categorical column, and value_counts on it keeps every category including the empty ones. Sort by the category order and build the dict with int() values.

choices: Turns a numeric column into labelled bands
questions.explain: Which is what lets you count a continuous measurement, where every raw value would otherwise be its own group.

questions.prompt: How many edges do four bands need?
questions.explain: Each band sits between two edges, so there is always one more edge than label.

questions.prompt: Which side of a band does a boundary value fall on, by default?
choices: The lower band — the right edge belongs to its band
questions.explain: Bands are right-inclusive by default, which is why grade edges are written at 69, 79 and 89 rather than 70, 80 and 90.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between cut and qcut?
choices: cut makes equal-width bands; qcut makes bands with roughly equal counts
questions.explain: They answer different questions, and on skewed data they look very different.
